rich_summary: This section recounts the divine births of the first two Pandavas and the events leading toward the birth of a third. At Pandu’s request, Kunti uses the sacred incantation given by the sage Durvasa to summon the god of justice, Dharma. From their union is born Yudhishthira, foretold by a heavenly voice to be the most virtuous of men and a future ruler. Pandu then asks for a son of immense physical power, leading Kunti to invoke Vayu, the wind-god, who fathers Bhima. Bhima’s extraordinary strength is revealed immediately when he falls from Kunti’s lap and shatters a rock without harm. Significantly, Bhima is born on the same day as Duryodhana. Pandu then resolves to obtain an even greater son through austerities to please Indra, foreshadowing the birth of Arjuna.

highlight_spans.why: Introduces the moral dilemma and Pandu’s request that Kunti summon a celestial being for offspring.

top_scenes.scene_text: The god of justice appears in radiant splendor before Kunti as she performs sacred incantations, sunlight-like brilliance surrounding his celestial chariot.
Infant Bhima falls from Kunti’s lap onto a mountain rock that shatters into fragments while the unharmed child lies amid the broken stone.
King Pandu stands on one leg in harsh wilderness austerity, meditating intensely to please Indra while sages watch from the forest.
